paper: Kassam & Trefethen, Fourth-Order Time-Stepping for Stiff PDEs, SISC 26(4):1214-1233, 2005

open_questions.q: Does the contour-integral evaluation of the ETDRK4 phi-function coefficients remain uniformly machine-accurate when the linear operator L is non-diagonal (e.g. Chebyshev-spectral discretizations, non-normal L, or Jacobian linearizations of nonlinear-diffusion problems), rather than diagonal in a Fourier basis?
open_questions.basis: The paper's contour trick and our replication both diagonalize L (Fourier basis) and average the integrand over a circle around each scalar eigenvalue hL. For a non-diagonal L one must either evaluate phi(hL) as a matrix function via contour integration in the resolvent, or diagonalize a non-normal L (which can be catastrophically ill-conditioned). The paper mentions Chebyshev briefly but our replication only covers Fourier + diagonal L; the numerical stability of the contour cure in the non-diagonal / non-normal regime is not established here.
next_steps: Implement a Chebyshev-spectral test problem (e.g. Allen-Cahn on [-1,1] with Dirichlet BCs) and evaluate phi_k(hL) via a matrix-valued contour integral around the numerical range of hL.

Compare accuracy vs (a) direct matrix exponential via scaling-and-squaring and (b) Krylov-subspace phi approximations across a sweep of |hL| including operators with pseudospectra extending far from the eigenvalues.
Report both forward error (against a high-precision reference) and the effective condition number of the eigenvector basis to characterize when contour evaluation degrades.

open_questions.q: Is ETDRK4 (Cox-Matthews) genuinely competitive on a work-precision basis against modern IMEX-RK schemes (e.g. ARK4(3)6L[2]SA of Kennedy-Carpenter) and operator-splitting methods (Strang / Yoshida) on the same stiff PDE benchmarks, once cost-per-step is charged?
open_questions.basis: Our replication (and the paper's headline) compares ETDRK4 vs IFRK4 only, at equal step size, and reports 1.4x-5.1x error advantages for ETDRK4. Neither the paper nor this replication provides wall-clock or FLOP-normalized comparisons against IMEX-RK or split-step, which are the practical competitors on stiff semilinear problems today. Without a work-precision study the accuracy advantage does not translate into a clear practical recommendation.
next_steps: Add IMEX-RK (ARK4) and Strang-split integrators to work/integrators.py.
Run each on KS / Burgers / Allen-Cahn / KdV over a sweep of tolerances and record error vs (wall-clock, RHS evals, FFT count).
Plot Pareto fronts; report where ETDRK4 dominates, is dominated, or ties, and identify the stiffness / spectral-gap regimes that determine the winner.

open_questions.q: Do higher-order ETD-RK schemes (ETDRK5, ETDRK6, or Krogstad-family fifth/sixth-order variants) yield a favorable accuracy-per-cost tradeoff for the same stiff PDEs, or does the growing count of phi-function coefficients (each requiring its own contour evaluation) and the added Butcher-stage RHS work erase the gain?
open_questions.basis: The paper studies fourth-order variants only (Cox-Matthews and Krogstad). Higher-order ETD-RK formulations exist in the literature but require more phi-function coefficients (phi_0,...,phi_p for order p) and more stages, which multiplies both contour-integration cost and per-step RHS evaluations. Whether the theoretical order gain survives in practice on stiff semilinear PDEs is not addressed by the paper or this replication.
next_steps: Derive or transcribe the phi-coefficient formulas for a candidate ETDRK5 (e.g. Luan-Ostermann or a 5th-order Krogstad variant).
Extend etdrk4_coeffs() to a general etdrk_coeffs(order, L, h, M) that evaluates all required phi_k on the same contour.
Repeat the C3/C4 convergence and error-ratio study, adding a wall-clock axis, and check whether ETDRK5/6 dominates ETDRK4 on any benchmark for realistic tolerances (e.g. 1e-8 to 1e-12).

open_questions.q: Does the ETDRK4-with-contour approach retain its accuracy and stability advantages on quasi-linear / nonlinear-diffusion PDEs (e.g. porous-medium u_t = (u^m)_xx, Cahn-Hilliard, or reaction-diffusion with a solution-dependent diffusivity D(u))?
open_questions.basis: The paper's four benchmarks (KS, Burgers, Allen-Cahn, KdV) all have a linear stiff operator L that is fixed in advance and diagonalizable in Fourier space. Quasi-linear problems have L = L(u(t)) that changes each step; a naive freeze-and-recompute strategy would require recomputing E, E2, Q, f1, f2, f3 (i.e. running the contour integration) at every step, potentially erasing the efficiency case. Neither the paper nor this replication tests this class of problems.
next_steps: Implement a quasi-linear benchmark (e.g. porous-medium with m=2, or Cahn-Hilliard with variable mobility) with a rebuild-L-each-step ETDRK4 driver.
Measure (a) order of convergence, (b) error and stability at moderate stiffness, and (c) per-step cost including contour re-evaluation.
Compare against a Rosenbrock-W or Newton-Krylov implicit integrator on the same problems to see whether the exponential-integrator advantage survives when L must be rebuilt each step.

open_questions.q: For the contour-integral evaluation of the phi-function coefficients, what is the optimal contour radius r and quadrature count M as functions of hL, spectral radius, and target precision, and can adaptive choice of (r, M) tighten the accuracy floor below the current ~1e-15 fp64 wall?
open_questions.basis: Our replication uses M=32 quadrature nodes on the unit circle (r=1) uniformly across all eigenvalues, giving max contour error ~3e-15 for f1 (near the fp64 machine wall). The paper suggests M=32 as a robust default but does not derive an optimal (r, M) rule as a function of |hL| or spectral shape, and does not discuss how to break through the fp64 floor when higher precision is required (e.g. reference-quality solutions, extended-precision studies).
next_steps: Sweep (r, M) over a grid at fixed hL and characterize the error surface; derive an empirical rule r*(|hL|), M*(target eps).
Implement mpmath-precision (dps=50-100) contour evaluation and quantify the achievable coefficient accuracy vs M for extended precision.
For fp64, test adaptive M per eigenvalue (small M for large |hL| where direct is already accurate; large M only near the cancellation region) and quantify the total FFT / phi-eval cost savings.
